# Sunday Serif

> A soft serif for slow days. Free and open-source (SIL Open Font License 1.1, Reserved Font Name "Sunday Serif"), with print effects on variable axes. Made by Federico Kratter Thaler for Sunday (https://joinsunday.co).

- Website: https://sunday-serif.kkratter.com
- Source and issues: https://github.com/kkratterf/sunday-serif
- Downloads (desktop and web fonts): https://github.com/kkratterf/sunday-serif/releases/latest
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/sunday-serif

## Family

- Families: "Sunday Serif" (roman and italic). Weights Regular 400, Medium 500, SemiBold 600, Bold 700.
- Variable axes (same in roman and italic):
  - wght, Weight, 400 to 700, default 400
  - BURN, Light Burn, 0 to 100, default 0. Towards 100 the ink floods the letters, like an overexposed print.
  - INKB, Ink Bleed, 0 to 100, default 0. Puffy, organic letters as if the ink spread into the paper; spacing never changes.
  - WORN, Worn Print, 0 to 100, default 0. Grain eating the edges, dust specks and starved patches of missing ink, growing towards 100; spacing never changes.
- Sunday Serif Grain: a separate display family (roman and italic, Regular only) with one axis, GRAN, Grain Blur, 0 to 100, default 0. A blur made of grain: towards 100 a cloud of ink dots spreads out from every edge; spacing never changes.
- Character set: Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended-A. Features: kern, case, ordn, ccmp.

## Files

- Desktop: variable/SundaySerif[BURN,INKB,WORN,wght].ttf and SundaySerif-Italic[BURN,INKB,WORN,wght].ttf, plus SundaySerifGrain[GRAN].ttf and SundaySerifGrain-Italic[GRAN].ttf; static otf/ and ttf/ for Regular, Medium, SemiBold and italics (effects at 0).
- Web (WOFF2, 1000 UPM): SundaySerifText-Variable.woff2 and SundaySerifText-Italic-Variable.woff2 (wght only, about 55 KB, for text); SundaySerif-Variable.woff2 and SundaySerif-Italic-Variable.woff2 (all four axes, about 1.8 MB, only where effects show); SundaySerifGrain-Variable.woff2 and SundaySerifGrain-Italic-Variable.woff2 (Grain Blur, about 1.5 MB, display only).
- Mobile (React Native, Expo): use the static TTFs; React Native cannot set custom variable axes.

## Use on the web

- npm: `pnpm add sunday-serif`, then `import "sunday-serif/text.css"` (family "Sunday Serif") and, only where effects show, `import "sunday-serif/fx.css"` (family "Sunday Serif FX"); for Grain Blur, `import "sunday-serif/grain.css"` (family "Sunday Serif Grain", axis "GRAN").
- Next.js: `import { SundaySerif, SundaySerifFX } from "sunday-serif/next"`, put `${SundaySerif.variable} ${SundaySerifFX.variable}` on <html>, then use `var(--font-sunday-serif)` and `var(--font-sunday-serif-fx)`. `SundaySerifGrain` sets `var(--font-sunday-serif-grain)`.
- Weight with `font-weight: 400` to `600`. Effects with `font-variation-settings: "BURN" 0, "INKB" 0, "WORN" 0;` (tags upper case and quoted). Setting font-variation-settings replaces the whole list, so always set all three effects together, e.g. through CSS custom properties.

## Working on the repository

- Rules for contributors and AI agents: https://github.com/kkratterf/sunday-serif/blob/main/AGENTS.md
- Build: `make` (needs uv), checks: `make test` (fontbakery). Sources are UFO masters with two designspace files in sources/.
